prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” broker for every self‑employed person — the right choice depends on your budget, whether you want in‑person service, if you qualify for Medicaid/subsidies, and what networks or doctors you need. Rather than a single name, here’s how to find the best broker for you in Kansas City, MO, plus practical options and what to ask.

Quick options to consider
- Local independent health insurance agents/brokers: they can compare plans from multiple carriers and often provide ongoing service. Look for someone licensed in Missouri and experienced with ACA individual/family plans.  
- National online brokers/marketplaces: eHealth, HealthSherpa, GoHealth and HealthMarkets can be convenient for comparing plans and subsidies online.  
- Government resources: Healthcare.gov (or the Missouri Exchange) has a list of certified agents and navigators who can help enroll you in ACA plans and check subsidy eligibility.  
- Community navigators or nonprofits: free help for enrollment and assessing Medicaid eligibility (Missouri has Medicaid expansion).

How to find reputable local brokers
- Use the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance license lookup to confirm an agent/broker is licensed.  
- Search the National Association of Health Underwriters (NAHU) directory for certified brokers in KC.  
- Check reviews (Google, Facebook, Yelp) and ask other self‑employed people or small business owners for referrals.  
- Prefer an independent broker (not captive to one carrier) so you get multiple carriers/plan types.

Questions to ask any broker before committing
- Are you licensed in Missouri and appointed with major carriers that serve Kansas City?  
- Do you specialize in individual/ACA plans for self‑employed clients? How long have you done this?  
- Do you charge me any fees, or do you earn commissions from the insurer? (Most do not charge consumers for individual plans.)  
- Will you help with subsidy calculations, enrollments, and any year‑round changes (life events, renewals, claims help)?  
- Which carriers/plans do you typically recommend for someone with my needs? (Describe budget, preferred doctors, prescriptions.)  
- Can you provide references from other self‑employed clients?

Other things to consider for self‑employed people
- Check whether you qualify for ACA premium tax credits (subsidies) through Healthcare.gov.  
- If you have low income, confirm Medicaid eligibility in Missouri.  
- If you want dental/vision, ask brokers to include those quotes.  
- If you have contractors/employees and want a small-group plan instead, say so up front.

If you want, I can:
- Find highly rated Kansas City brokers/agents (I’ll need your ZIP code and whether you prefer in‑person or remote help).  
- Or prepare a short script/email you can send to 3–5 brokers to compare responses.

Which would you prefer?
